clue.text: Senior detectives excuse certain offence

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, senior police detectives
a plea is an excuse offered in defence
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Top police officers decide that some crime is excusable, or perhaps excuse one particular crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking offence is feeling annoyance or disapproval, the same feeling as being put out by something.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing compiler had line with Queen

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, I; 'I had' contracts to I'd
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A useless setter wrote a line about the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout who does no work is a lazy, worthless person, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Forgiving one found in clear

indicators.note: the single numeral is found within the word for clear, so one goes inside another

parts.note: patent means obvious or clear
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A merciful person turns up in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forbearing and tolerant of others' faults puts up with delay and annoyance calmly.

clue.text: Assemble Mercedes securing badge

indicators.note: the words Assemble Mercedes hold the answer fast within their letters, running across the word break

explanation.surface: Put together a Mercedes car with its bonnet badge fixed on.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a symbolic device or badge, like a car maker's logo.

clue.text: More revealing view seen on stage

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to scan is to look over or view
a tier is a level or stage

explanation.surface: A theatre critic notes that a more risque show can be watched on the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpier clothing covers less, so scantier outfits show more of the body.

clue.text: Break sleep embracing devoted sweetheart

indicators.note: the word for sleep wraps its arms round the word for devoted, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: rest means sleep
PI, short for pious, means devoted or religious
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A short nap takes in a devoted loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short pause or interval of relief, a break from something hard.

clue.text: Basement's hit in explosion burying large foundation

indicators.note: the letter for large is buried inside the rearranged letters
blown apart, the letters of basement's and hit are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the possessive S is kept as a letter here, giving the word with an S

explanation.surface: A bomb in a cellar blows up and buries a big building's base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in explosion' rearranges BASEMENTS and HIT; 'burying' places L (large) among them.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment is an institution that has been founded, such as a school or a charity: a foundation.

clue.text: Tip about a pound for fancy man

indicators.note: the word for tip goes round the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: to tip a jug is to pour from it
to ram is to pound or batter

explanation.surface: A tipster offers a pound bet on some fancied man, like a horse racing tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit lover, and a fancy man is a woman's lover in old slang.

clue.text: Careless criminal team imprisoned by smart judge

indicators.note: the criminal and team are locked up between the words for smart and judge

parts.note: in means fashionable or smart
to rate is to judge or assess
a con is a convict, a criminal
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A crooked gang is jailed by a sharp judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thoughtless of other people's feelings is carelessness toward them.

clue.text: Crown's upset about London leader in foreign city

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the London letter
upset means turned over, so the word for crowns is read backwards

parts.note: a tip is the crown or top; crown's read as crown is, with the S kept, gives the plural

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of London

explanation.surface: The monarchy is overturned, regarding a London leader abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TIPS into SPIT, and 'about' puts L, London's leader, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is a port city on the Croatian coast, so foreign to a British setter.

clue.text: Crew leader sat in bow disturbed surrounding area

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the letter for area
disturbed letters are shaken up, so sat in bow is rearranged

explanation.surface: The officer in charge of the sailors sat in the bows, upset, overseeing the space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges SATINBOW, and 'surrounding' puts A (area) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun is the ship's officer in charge of the deck hands, leading the crew.

clue.text: A refined man accepts mere tailored fitting

indicators.note: the gentleman takes in the rearranged letters, so they go inside

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a refined man

indicators.note: tailored means altered to fit, so the letters of mere are recut

explanation.surface: A smart gentleman receives a fitting from a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailored fitting' reads as a suit being measured, but 'tailored' is the anagram signal and 'fitting' alone is the definition, in its sense of matching.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting can mean being in accord or matching, which is what concord or accord describes.

clue.text: Initially insect metamorphosed and got out

definitions.text: Initially insect metamorphosed and got out

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: A bug changed shape and emerged from its cocoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final adult stage of an insect, reached after metamorphosis when it emerges.

clue.text: Delayed housing over cold spot

indicators.note: the word for delayed houses the two letters inside it

parts.note: late means delayed
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A delayed arrival shelters from a chilly patch.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to find or pinpoint where it is.

clue.text: Drink for winners capturing hero's heart

indicators.note: the word for winners captures the middle letters, holding them inside

parts.note: champs are champions, winners

indicators.note: heart means the central part, so the middle two letters of hero are taken

parts.note: hero's reads as the possessive of hero, the word whose middle is taken

explanation.surface: Fizz for the victors wins the hero over.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is British slang for champagne, the traditional celebratory drink.

clue.text: Ample nurse goes nearly crazy

indicators.note: crazy letters are jumbled, so nurse and the shortened goes are rearranged
nearly means not quite the whole word, so the last letter of goes is dropped

explanation.surface: A buxom nurse is almost going mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts GOES to GOE, and 'crazy' rearranges NURSE with GOE.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous helping is a large, plentiful one, so ample in amount.

clue.text: Stand to top very big gangster's offer

indicators.note: in a down clue, to top means placed above the rest

parts.note: a prop is a support or stand
OS is the clothing size outsize, very big
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster; gangster's reads as gangster is

explanation.surface: A huge mobster makes a bid to outdo his rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for acceptance, a suggestion or offer.

clue.text: Strong opening taking practically all wickets

indicators.note: the word for opening takes in the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a start is an opening or beginning

indicators.note: practically means almost, so the last letter of all is lost

parts.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wickets

explanation.surface: A sturdy start to a cricket match sees a bowler claim nearly every wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practically' and 'taking' work on 'all wickets', which looks like a cricket phrase but splits into a clipped word and the scorecard letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart means sturdy and dependable, firmly built and robust.

clue.text: More frail and tiny pass on resistance

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny
to pass on is a euphemism for to die
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A sickly little person passes away despite fighting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Weedy describes someone thin and weak, so the comparative means feebler.

clue.text: Gutted after opening for Spurs got a goal

indicators.note: the word for gutted comes after the opening letter
the opening of Spurs is its first letter

parts.note: cored means with the inside removed, gutted

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur, known as Spurs, were devastated after conceding, then struck back with a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' looks like British slang for bitterly disappointed but means hollowed out here.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, to score is to get a goal; the past tense matches the clue's tense.

clue.text: Equipment belt?

definitions.meaning: British slang for gear, kit or belongings
to strike someone hard, to wallop

explanation.surface: A query whether a belt counts as kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both British slang for one's gear and a verb for hitting hard.

clue.text: Good health? Mine's swallowing endless red!

indicators.note: the mine swallows the shortened colour word, holding it inside

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine; the 's reads as is

indicators.note: endless says to remove the last letter of the word

parts.note: rosy means red or pink

explanation.surface: A toast is raised as a miner downs most of a glass of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' and 'swallowing' act on 'red', which suggests wine in the surface but is only a colour word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a Latin-derived drinking toast wishing health, like cheers.

clue.text: Chart the French Canadian symbol's origin

parts.note: a map is a chart
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Charting the source of a French-Canadian emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition takes a moment: the Canadian symbol is the leaf on the flag, and this tree is where that leaf comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The red leaf on Canada's flag comes from this tree, so the tree is the emblem's source.

clue.text: Part of trapper for mercurial actor

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A role in a play about a temperamental fur trapper goes to a thespian.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a stage or screen artist, one kind of entertainer who plays for an audience.

clue.text: Perfect half of family raised in criminal society

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: A1 means first-class or perfect, written with I for the figure one

indicators.note: half of takes the first three of the six letters of family

explanation.surface: An ideal half of a family is brought up within a crime gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AIFAM (AI plus FAM, half of family) upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is the organised crime network originating in Sicily, a secret criminal brotherhood.

clue.text: Young man who, on reflection, went west?

definitions.text: Young man who, on reflection, went west?

parts.words: Young man who, on reflection, went west?
parts.note: the Greek youth fell in love with his reflection in a pool and wasted away; to go west is slang for to die

explanation.surface: A young man thinks things over and heads off to America's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' seems to mean after thinking, but means while gazing at his image; 'went west' means died.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the beautiful youth pined away gazing at his own image, and a flower grew in his place.

clue.text: Boring thing, holding iron over suit

indicators.note: the boring tool holds the turned letters inside it

parts.note: a bit is the drilling tip that bores holes

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the iron symbol is read backwards

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A dull man clutching a golf club wears a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to be appropriate for, as when a thing suits someone.

clue.text: Real patriot agitated working classes

indicators.note: agitated letters are stirred up, so real patriot is rearranged

explanation.surface: A true nationalist rouses the labouring masses.
explanation.definitionFit: The proletariat is Marx's term for wage-earning workers, the labouring classes.
